plainName: Deductions from income from house property
summary: From a house's annual value a fixed share is deducted, whatever you actually spent, and then the interest payable on money you borrowed to buy, build, repair or rebuild it. Interest for the years before the house was bought or built is spread over the year it was and the following years. For a house valued at nil as your own residence, the interest and the spread-out interest are together limited: a higher limit where the house was bought or built in time with the loan and the lender certifies the interest, a lower one otherwise, and one limit across all such houses. In the default regime the current interest on your own residence is not deducted.

routes.name: The fixed share
routes.description: A fixed share of the annual value, never actual expenses.

routes.name: Interest on a let or unlet house
routes.description: The interest payable for the year, deducted in full.

routes.name: Interest before the house was bought or built
routes.description: Spread in equal parts over the year of acquisition or completion and the following years.

routes.name: Interest on your own residence
routes.description: The interest and the spread-out interest, together within the limits.

disqualifiers.description: The current interest on your own residence is not deducted in the default regime.
Without the lender's certificate of the interest, your own residence gets only the lower limit.
A loan for repairs, or a house not bought or built in time after the borrowing, gets only the lower limit.
Interest you deduct as a first-home loan deduction may not be deducted here again.
Deductions above the income of the head would make a loss.

enforcedBy.reason: Not built yet: setting off a loss under this head comes with set-off.
